source.author: lucan
source.text: - Zephyros quoque vana vetustas His ascribit aquis, quorum stata tempora flatus Continuique dies, et in aera longa potestas: Vel quod ab occiduo pellunt tot nubila coelo Trans Noton, et fluvio cogunt incumbere nimbos: Vel quod aquas toties rumpentis litora Nili Assiduo feriunt, coguntque resistere fluctus Ille mora cursus adversique obiice ponti Aestuat in campos.
source.text_original: - Zephyros quoque vana vetustas / His ascribit aquis, quorum stata tempora flatus / Continuique dies, et in aera longa potestas: / Vel quod ab occiduo pellunt tot nubila coelo / Trans Noton, et fluvio cogunt incumbere nimbos: / Vel quod aquas toties rumpentis litora Nili / Assiduo feriunt, coguntque resistere fluctus / Ille mora cursus adversique obiice ponti / Aestuat in campos.
source.text_english: Ancient legend also assigns the Zephyrs to these waters, whose breezes have fixed seasons, whose days of blowing are unbroken, and whose long dominion extends through the air: either because they drive so many clouds from the western sky beyond Notus, and force the storms to lean upon the river; or because they so often strike the shores of Nile, which bursts its banks, and compel the waves to stand still. There the sea boils over into the plains through delay in its course and the obstacle of the opposing bridge.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nil animi, nil regna iuvant; fremit obice ponti clausa cohors telisque salum facibusque coruscat.
reuse.text_original: nil animi, nil regna iuvant; fremit obice ponti / clausa cohors telisque salum facibusque coruscat.
reuse.text_english: Neither courage nor kingdoms help; the enclosed host roars at the barrier of the sea, and the swell flashes with weapons and torches.
